title: BITLUME: Precision-Flexible Photonic Computing for Ultra-Fast and Energy-Efficient DNN Acceleration
problem: Silicon photonics for deep learning acceleration faces precision challenges due to noise and non-idealities, limiting practical deployment for high-precision computations. Electronic accelerators are reaching performance and energy limits for emerging applications.
motivation: Photonics offers superior bandwidth and energy efficiency for neural network acceleration, but precision limitations prevent adoption for workloads requiring >8-bit precision.
method: Proposes BITLUME, a photonic computing unit enabling multiplications beyond 8-bit precision through a precision-flexible scheme. Introduces optimized round-truncation algorithm and data mapping strategy to reduce optoelectronic conversions, enhance data reuse, and maintain accuracy. Develops hybrid optoelectronic architecture integrating BITLUME with FPGA, RF, and photonic components.
key_novelty: First precision-flexible photonic computing unit supporting variable precision DNN acceleration with 3.7× lower latency than A100 GPU on dot-product operations.
contributions: Precision-flexible photonic computing unit supporting variable-precision multiplications
Round-truncation algorithm optimizing optoelectronic conversions and data reuse
Hybrid optoelectronic architecture with up to 3.35× speedup and 1.53× energy savings vs. photonic accelerators, and 10.78× speedup, 4.12× energy savings vs. A100 GPU
limitations: Evaluation on FP32 DNN training; noise characteristics and precision degradation under process variation not detailed; scalability to larger networks not discussed.
